rules.R3_band: buildable N in [max(20, N_min), min(34, N_max)]; empty band = no design in that cell
rules.R4_parallel: Sp_max = floor(40 / (1.25 * Isc)) strings a tracker; fuses needed when Sp >= 3 or (Sp-1)*1.25*Isc > the declared module fuse rating
rules.R5_volt_drop: volt drop pct = Imp * R / (N * Vmp * (1 + gamma/100 * (Thot - 25))) * 100 <= 1.5; R = r_lead*N*0.63 + r_site*((N-2)p + s + 2L) + (N+1)*Rc; monotone in L, so the SHORTEST home run in a band decides whether that band holds a design at all
rules.R6_wiring: conductor metres: sequential = 0.63N + (N-2)p + s + 2L; leapfrog-turned = 2.006N + 2L. Turned costs about 1.09 m of lead for every 1 m of site cable it saves, so it NEVER minimises metres; it only wins on resistance when r_lead / r_site < ((N-2)p + s) / (N * (2p - s + 0.2 - 0.63)), which at N=30, p=1.323 is 0.917 - i.e. only when the lead is a size larger than the site cable
rules.tie_break: the pack maximises N, then minimises conductor metres, then takes the largest lead size and the largest strings-in-parallel that still hold (metres do not depend on cable size, so that tie is settled by cross-section)

limits: The cold-voltage clause is DISPUTED. BOTH readings are computed everywhere: reading A adds a +10 K allowance to the site minimum, reading B does not. A design that holds on A but not on B is returned as DISPUTED-COLD-VOLTAGE, never as a bare pass.
Module pitch, junction-box spacing 0.84 m, 0.1 m lead slack, the 0.63 m supplied lead pair and the 45 m mean home run are ASSUMED (from the bench), not measured.
Vmp temperature coefficient is ASSUMED equal to the published Pmax coefficient; no class publishes a Vmp coefficient.
Ampacity is NOT checked here: the volt-drop cap of 1.5 % binds before the current-carrying table on every conductor in this space.
The inverter backfeed contribution to a string fault is not published, so the fuse answer is the parallel-string term only.
No rating is claimed beyond the declared tables. No maker, model or price appears anywhere.
bifacial factor 1.0..1.2 is applied to Isc for the design current and to Imp for the loss terms; it is a declared input, not a measured gain.
CPU watts were NOT measured - no wall meter and no RAPL read on this machine.
